title: Temporary Access, Data Escrow & Evidence Preservation Procedure (Draft)
body:
PURPOSE
This draft captures a practical, negotiable procedure and contract language options for: temporary customer or regulator access to customer-specific inference logs, model artifacts, and limited production telemetry; contractual data escrow deliverables in incident or insolvency scenarios; and formal evidence-preservation (legal hold) obligations tied to audits, litigation, or regulatory investigations.

SCOPE
Applies to: Hosted API customers, Dedicated customers where Redwood controls the serving, and Private deployments where Redwood provides emergency or on-prem evidence packages under a contractual obligation. Does NOT change existing GDPR/DPA terms except where explicitly referenced.

KEY PRINCIPLES (short)
- Minimize live-system blast radius: prefer snapshot-and-transfer over granting live access.
- Least privilege and time-bounded access.
- Chain-of-custody and integrity checks for any evidence handed over.
- Clear allocation of costs (Redwood vs customer) and notice timelines.

DEFINITIONS (short)
- Escrow Materials: repository of artifacts we agree to escrow (example list below).
- Temporary Access Window: limited, pre-approved timebox for remote or in-person access.
- Preservation Hold: suspension of normal deletion/retention policies for specified data sets.

ESCROW DELIVERABLES (suggested baseline list)
- Redacted query logs (time-ranged) or encrypted archive containing: request IDs, timestamps, route/model invoked, response length metrics; PII redacted per DPA specification.
- Model weights and config snapshots (if contractually required for insolvency / migration).
- Deployment manifests and pinned model-version map.
- Audit log extract (authN/authZ events) tied to access.
- Checksum manifest and transfer checksum file (SHA256).
- Transfer method options: SFTP to customer-controlled bucket; encrypted AWS S3 presigned URL; physical encrypted disk shipped under chain-of-custody.

ACCESS MODES (ranked by safety)
1) Export snapshot delivered to customer escrow environment (preferred).
2) Remote read-only session to sanitized environment with session recording + observer.
3) On-premises handover for Private deployments (customer-managed).
4) Live console access to Redwood production (only under extreme emergency, requires legal sign-off and SRE escort).

CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY & INTEGRITY CHECKS (operational steps)
- Generate archive -> compute SHA256 -> notarize with internal evidence ticket (link to ticket id) -> encrypt with customer public key -> transfer -> customer confirms checksum and receipt -> Redwood logs handover event with witness.
- All steps to be recorded in the EVIDENCE_HANDOVER ticket template (JIRA).

CONTRACT LANGUAGE – OPTIONS (two variants; include as negotiable snippets)
A) Minimal enterprise-friendly clause (for standard SaaS customers)
"In the event of a reasonably documented regulatory request, Redwood shall, upon receipt of written request from Customer and subject to applicable law, provide a time-limited data export or temporary, read-only access to Production Logs and related artifacts as specified in Schedule X. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to redact Personal Data in accordance with the DPA. Access will be time-boxed and may be subject to an access fee as set forth in the Order Form."

Negotiation notes: customers often request 'live access' and full raw logs — push back with snapshot + redaction, and require a mutual NDA for exploratory live sessions.

B) Escrow + insolvency transfer clause (for customers requiring migration guarantees)
"Upon Customer's written request in the event of Provider insolvency, material breach, or as otherwise set forth in the Order Form, Provider shall deliver the Escrow Materials to Customer or Customer's designated escrow agent within thirty (30) days. Delivery shall be via encrypted transfer and accompanied by integrity checks. Customer will bear costs of transfer unless otherwise agreed."

Negotiation notes: customers ask for exact model weights and training data. Red flag: training data transfer and IP leakage. Recommend: limit to model config & compiled artifacts sufficient to run inference, exclude training datasets.

PRESERVATION HOLD – TEMPLATE NOTICE (operational)
[Date]
To: Records & Compliance, Engineering, SRE, Cloud Operations
Subject: Preservation Hold — [Ticket/Case ID] — [Customer or Regulator Name]
Reason: [e.g., regulatory inquiry, litigation hold]
Scope: Preserve logs and archives matching the attached query (date range, customer-id, route filters). Do NOT delete or overwrite snapshots until hold is lifted.
Requested by: [Legal contact / Regulator liaison]
Duration: Until written release by Requestor or 90 days by default pending escalation.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED (for legal + infra)
- PII redaction standards: use case-by-case vs. standard pseudonymization pattern? Need definitive list of fields considered PII for exports.
- Cost model: per-GB extraction fee vs fixed-tier (customers push for no-fee for compliance requests).
- SLA for delivery: 7 days? 30 days? Legal prefers 30; customers often want faster for audits. Consider tiered (emergency vs routine).
- Insurance / liability carveouts if handover introduces vulnerability.

TECHNICAL CONTROLS CHECKLIST (for SRE/infra before any handover)
- Confirm snapshots exclude non-required tenant data.
- Verify encryption-at-rest and in-transit.
- Run malware scan on archives.
- Perform integrity checksum and notarize.
- Enable session recording for any remote access and store in evidence bucket.

EVIDENCE-SPECIFIC METRICS / LOG FIELDS (suggested minimal fields)
- request_id, customer_id, route_name, model_id, timestamp_utc, latency_ms, response_length_tokens, truncated_flag, redaction_marker

RISK MITIGATIONS & ESCALATION PATHS
- If customer demands raw user prompts with PII: require a court order or customer-signed waiver; escalate to GC and Privacy lead.
- If regulatory subpoena conflicts with fuller DPA commitments: follow lawfulness hierarchy; notify customer unless prohibited.

COST/BILLING (draft approach)
- Routine compliance export: included up to X GB/year; overage billed at $Y/GB.
- For bespoke escrow packaging (e.g., model artifacts + deployment manifests): flat fee + transfer costs.
- Emergency on-call SRE escort: hourly rate with minimum 4 hours.

REVIEW & APPROVAL CHECKPOINTS
- Legal: approve clause language and final escrow list.
- Privacy: approve PII redaction standard.
- Engineering: validate exportability and checklist.
- Sales/Account: confirm commercial terms and any customer concessions.

ACTION ITEMS (next steps)
- [ ] Legal to pick preferred contract snippet and produce a short plain-language summary for sales (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Engineering to define export format and produce mock export example (owner: Marcus).
- [ ] Privacy to define PII field list and redaction algorithm recommendations (owner: Elena).
- [ ] Ops to create JIRA template for EVIDENCE_HANDOVER and chain-of-custody checklist (owner: Noah).

NOTES / SCRATCHES (informal)
- Quick thought: offer a standardized "compliance tier" add-on that bundles 3 exports/yr + 48hr SLA — could simplify negotiations.
- Keep in mind Private deployments: many matters become customer's ops; still need evidence package play for support retention.
- Consider including sample checksum signing with KMS for high-assurance customers.

REFERENCES
- Internal: Confluence playbook (linked), DPA v2.1, Incident response runbook.
- External: ISO 27043 guidelines (for digital evidence), typical escrow service providers' templates.

END DRAFT

(Notes: this is intentionally practical not fully redlined legal language. We want a short, negotiable set of options that legal + eng can convert into final contract exhibits and SOW language.)
